LapKr — Product & Design Reference

Single-page spec document. It opens with the brand and product system — essence, wordmark, color, type, identity, coach, motion, app icon, UI conventions — then the product vision, terminology and locked requirements, and closes with each screen shown in dark and light over the hero background, the way it sits in the real app. Light theme is a derived proposal; the mock ships dark-only.

01 — Essence
Every tenth, explained.

LapKr is an AI karting telemetry platform. A driver uploads a session CSV; the Coach reads it and breaks down every corner, every braking zone, every tenth left on the table. It puts data-engineer-grade analysis in reach of the amateur karter — the driver who takes it seriously but has neither a sponsor nor $50-an-hour for a human coach.

02 — Wordmark
LapKr

Image or live type — both are canonical. The Kr uses a custom angular K in brand blue; the Lap recolors to dark on light surfaces while the Kr stays blue. Wherever “LapKr” appears as text it is always set in Neuropolitical with the logo colors — Lap follows the theme, Kr stays blue — rendered live here as LapKr (the face is embedded in this document). The two image files cover placements that need the original artwork, such as the splash.

lapkr-logo.png · on dark
lapkr-logo-on-light.png · on light
03 — Color System
Blue is data. Orange is the Coach.

The palette is semantic, not decorative. Blue marks data — best lap, scoreboard, links, following — and data values render as a 135° gradient from #3B82F6 into the lighter #93C5FD. Orange marks the Coach and every primary CTA: buttons are a vertical #F97316 → #EA580C gradient with a glow, while accent numbers and headlines (deltas, the hero word) run #FDBA74 → #F97316. Both ride on near-black #050505. Nav, sidebar and content cards are all one translucent white film (rgba(255,255,255,.10) + heavy blur) with no gradient of their own — on the hero-backed splash and login they transmit the blurred footage behind them; everywhere else they sit on the solid theme background. Only menus and popovers are solid #14141A; the driver's own feed card carries a faint orange tint.

Every swatch below is a flat, solid color so a picker can sample it cleanly. Where a color only exists inside a gradient, a hover state, or one specific surface, that is noted under the swatch — never baked into the chip.

04 — Typography
Two faces, no mono.

Chakra Petch carries display, KPIs and every number — lap times, RPM, speed. DM Sans carries body and UI. Labels never drop below 11px, body never below 12px; hero values may scale down but never under 22px. Readability floors: body text opacity ≥ .8, labels ≥ .7 — never below .5 on any readable text.

05 — Helmets & Hero
Five liveries, one badge.

Every driver picks a helmet; each carries the same LapKr badge on the rear panel. h01 Apex Blue is the flagship house livery. The hero footage (hero.mp4, a kart at sunset) backs the splash and the login flow — nowhere else. Every other screen sits on a solid theme background (resolved 2026-06-09): no frozen hero frame, no video.

Backgrounds
hero.mp4 backs the splash and the login flow only. Every other screen uses the solid theme background — resolved, no longer open.
h01 · Apex Blue
Electric blue, white pinstripes
Flagship
h02 · Carbon Edge
Matte carbon, single blue stripe
h03 · Sunset Strike
Fluorescent orange, zigzag decal
h04 · Heritage White
White, red center stripe
h05 · Stealth Lime
Gunmetal, lime accents

How a helmet reaches a driver. The picker opens at first-run signup — the driver must commit, no cancel — and reopens any time from Profile / Account via “Change helmet”. Assets ship in four square buckets (24, 48, 96, 200px); every surface loads the smallest bucket ≥ 2× its render size, so pixels stay retina-crisp without over-fetching. Drivers without a stored helmet id (other users, seed data) map deterministically to a livery: character-code sum of the display name, modulo 5.

06 — Coach
The AI that reads your laps.

Coach is the analysis engine, surfaced in orange. Its primary surface is the Coach chat — a drawer item that opens a bottom sheet (88vh) over the current screen, with reply tiers Quick · 2 cr, Standard · 4 cr, Deep · 5 cr and Ultra · 8 cr (partial 5 cr). It also appears as the pattern insight on the Dashboard and as the Coach zone inside Session Detail. It reads the parsed telemetry and returns corner-by-corner narrative, spends credits per run, and is powered by the Claude API (Opus/Sonnet). The driver profile it maintains over time is the DNA.

07 — Motion
Two curves. Three durations.

Motion is restrained: two easing curves, three durations, soft fade-ups. In this document the in-phone entrances and sheet slides run on the spec curves at preview-stretched durations — the 160/240/320ms tokens are the build values. Below are the patterns in motion, then the raw tokens.

Ease-out · cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1)
Reveal on scroll · 80ms stagger
Track-pin & marker-dot pulse
Wordmark rise-in · splash
Same move, three durations · --dur-fast 160ms · --dur-base 240ms · --dur-slow 320ms
Ease-in exit · cubic-bezier(.64,0,.78,0) — dismissals leave fast

The home-screen mark is the brand Kr — the same angular letterforms as the wordmark — on white. Installable as a PWA: standalone, portrait, theme and background #050505.

manifest.json
name LapKr — Telemetry Analysis · short_name LapKr · sizes 32 / 180 / 192 / 512 + maskable · display standalone · orientation portrait
09 — UI Conventions
Two-tier glass, everywhere.

Safe areas. Every screen respects device safe-area insets via env(safe-area-inset-*) (and the WindowInsets equivalent on Android). The top inset clears the status bar and any camera cutout — notch, Dynamic Island or in-screen punch-hole; scrolling media may run under it but interactive content never does. The bottom inset clears the iPhone home indicator and the Android gesture bar or 3-button nav; primary docks (auth buttons, CTAs) reserve this space. The left and right insets matter just as much: edge-to-edge and waterfall displays can clip or distort content at the physical edge, so every screen keeps a minimum lateral margin (14px in the maquettes) on top of env(safe-area-inset-left/right) — full-bleed surfaces (sheets, maps, video) may touch the edge but their CONTENT keeps the margin. Left and right insets apply in landscape. Camera placement varies by device, so the mockups show the range — a centered island, a left or right in-screen punch-hole, and devices whose camera and controls sit off the screen entirely (no in-screen cutout or home indicator).

Surfaces are one translucent white film , not flat fills and with no gradient of their own. The full recipe is below — background, 1px border, blur with saturation and shadow always travel together. On the hero-backed splash and login the film transmits the blurred footage; everywhere else it sits on the solid theme background. Only menus and popovers are solid #14141A; the driver's own feed card carries a faint orange tint. Panels round at 16px on a phone (fluid to 20px at desktop, --radius-panel); inner elements at 10px (fluid to 14px, --radius-inner). Chips are a colored dot plus an uppercase label. Primary CTAs are the orange gradient with a glow; secondary buttons are a faint white fill. Trust badges are a shield in the tier color. Seven breakpoints; touch targets never under 40px, form inputs never under 44px tall on mobile.

Canonical empty state (lk-empty-state) — the one cross-screen component every zero state reuses (Sessions, Garage, H2H, Profile): an 84×84 tile at radius 24 with an orange tint (rgba(249,115,22,.10) fill, .24 border) holding a 40×40 icon, a Chakra Petch 800 title, a DM Sans 14px body at .70, and the orange-gradient CTA. A --danger modifier recolors the tile for destructive contexts.

10 — Terminology
Canonical names.

The names the UI, code and docs all use — reconstructed from the TDD. One word per concept, no synonyms.

TermMeaning
SessionAn uploaded run — a CSV of laps for one kart at one track on one day.
LapA single timed circuit inside a session, with sector splits and telemetry.
SectorA timed segment of a lap used for split comparison.
PBPersonal Best — the driver's fastest lap for a track + category combo.
Kart / GarageA registered vehicle and its specs. The Garage holds the driver's karts; one is default.
ScoreboardRanked public leaderboard by track and category.
Credits / PackPrepaid units spent on AI analysis. Sold in five packs.
CoachThe in-app AI. Reads telemetry and returns corner-by-corner coaching.
DNAThe driver profile the Coach builds and maintains over time.
H2HHead-to-Head — a two-lap replay and telemetry comparison.
FeedThe social stream of sessions, PBs and achievements.
Trust tierConfidence label on a record: High, Moderate, Not verified.
11 — Product Requirements
Locked decisions.

The headline requirements distilled from the TDD — confirmed, not the full spec.

AreaLocked
Internationalization10 locales (EN ES IT PT-BR FR DE NL JA KO ZH-CN), every string keyed, all locales shipped together.
i18n formattingUnit symbols (°C, km/h, kg, mm, PSI, RPM) never translate. Decimal separator follows the locale — except lap times, always . (motorsport convention). Thousands separator per locale. Dates via Intl.DateTimeFormat. No RTL. Copy is verbatim from the i18n dictionaries — never invented.
Credit packs (USD)Quick $3.99 · Starter $9.99 · Racer $22.99 · Weekend $39.99 · Season $99.99.
Trust tiersHigh (AiM/MyChron CSV) · Moderate (LapKr CSV) · Not verified (manual). R1 ships Gate 1 live. Production targets blue High.
Telemetry channelsCanonical set: speed rpm throttle brake steering gear gforce_lat gforce_lon gps_lat gps_lon gps_alt.
AIClaude API — Opus/Sonnet for analysis narrative, Haiku for translation and moderation.
StackNext.js · Firebase (Auth / Firestore / Storage) · Cloud Run · Stripe · Leaflet maps.
SeedDefault kart Tony Kart Racer 401 / OK Senior. Helmet liveries h01–h05, h01 flagship.
Responsive7 breakpoints (xxl → xs-narrow), touch targets ≥40px, no page-level horizontal scroll.

Screen 01
Get Started — flow
No account: the Login screen offers Continue with Google or Continue with Apple — no separate sheet, no logo bar, no tagline. Right after signing in, the driver is asked to enable Face ID or fingerprint unlock. With biometrics enabled, reopening the app validates and goes straight to the Feed — there is no separate Welcome back screen; if skipped, reopening goes straight to the Feed too. Each screen dark and light: text over the video stays light in both modes, surfaces follow the theme. Copy verbatim from i18n; Face ID strings and the driver name are placeholders.

Screen 02
Feed
The driver's home. A scrollable feed of own and followed sessions grouped by day, each card showing track, kart, data logger, best lap and trust. On desktop the navigation rail and social rail sit left and right; on mobile they collapse into the hamburger and social drawers shown here. Own posts carry the orange tint; scoreboard posts carry the blue badge. Helmets are real liveries; data and copy verbatim from the mock.

Screen 03
Dashboard
The driver's home base. Plan and credits strip, five weekly KPIs, your top 3 laps with track maps, and an Achievements row that opens the full badge grid as its own view. On desktop the nav rail sits left; on mobile it collapses into the drawer (see Feed). Solid theme background, no hero. Data verbatim from the mock.
Navigation between sub-blocks
2.8 DrawerDashboard→3.1 DashboardAchievements row→3.3 Achievements←→3.1 Dashboard
3.1 is one continuous scrolling view — scroll inside the phone to reach its tail. 3.3 is its own view, entered from the Achievements row at the end of the scroll.

Screen 04
New Session
The session wizard behind the orange + button: pick a vehicle, choose Quick Upload or the Guided five-stage flow — Initial Setup, AI Proposed Setup with refine chat, Session with CSV upload, Post Session with the four feedback voices, and Finish with carry-over into the next session. AI costs verbatim: Propose 2 cr · Chat 2 cr · Feedback 5 cr.
Navigation between sub-blocks
Isla+ central→4.1 Vehiclepick kart→4.3 PathQuick Upload→4.4 Upload modal
4.3 PathGuided Session→4.11 Initial SetupPropose · 2 cr→4.14 ProposedApply & Continue→4.17 SessionCSV→4.18
4.18Next→4.22 Post SessionGenerate · 5 cr→4.24 FinishStart New Session→nuevo draft
4.22credits = 0→4.23 Out of credits
cualquier stage🗑 in the header→4.25 Discard
4.1empty garage→4.24.11propuesta viva→4.12Propose <4 fields→4.13
4.11Skip→4.154.14balance < 2 cr→4.16
4.17CSV invalid→4.194.17Next without CSV→4.20
Quick Upload opens the shared upload modal; on validation it redirects to the Session detail (SDV) and the draft is discarded. The wizard is an own view: no island and no top bar. The 5.1 draft card (Resume) re-enters this flow's saved stage. With an empty garage, 4.1 shows only the “Add a kart” CTA. States (2026-06-10): 4.2 copy verbatim i18n EN (wiz_vp_empty_body / wiz_vp_empty_cta “Add a vehicle” — the JS fallback says kart, i18n rules). 4.12 footer boolHasProp: Regenerate proposal · 2 cr (same cost) + Next without Skip. 4.13/4.20 = shared confirm modal (js/features/modals/confirm.js, with ✕): lowctx Stage 1 fires with <4 fields (the 3 in the body comes from the guard, the backdrop is illustrative) and Stage 3 with buildStage3LowctxBody branch both (0% from the seed). 4.15 = renderProposalEmptyState (orange→red gradient CTA verbatim .sdv-ai-empty-cta) + single footer Next: Session. 4.16 = renderCreditGuard: the interstitial replaces ONLY the input row, the thread stays visible. 4.19 = .wiz-csv-zone.is-invalid + upload_error_missing_columns; Browse stays active. 4.4 checked against upload-build.js: Upload pill, Telemetry file label outside the zone, Download LapKr CSV template link, submit disabled without a file; Unsupported file format state not represented (R2).

🏎️ Driver coaching
Smoother turn-in on T1
Less aggressive initial steering input — let the softer front bar do the rotation work instead of forcing it.
Confidence · High
🔧 Vehicle changes
Rear axle SOFT (Q)
One step softer to free rotation. Expect ~0.10s gain on flowing sectors.
Confidence · High
Front torsion bar SOFT
More front grip on entry. May feel slightly less sharp on initial turn-in.
Confidence · Medium
Cold rear pressures −0.2 psi
Widens contact patch. Monitor wear pattern — risk of increased degradation if pressures drop too far.
Confidence · Medium
Seat 1 cm rearward
Shifts weight toward rear axle to complement softer rear.
Confidence · Low

Feedback
Overview · DriverSolid session — best lap improved by 0.4s vs previous visit. Consistency σ dropped from 0.31 to 0.22. Main time loss sits in mid-corner on T3 and T8 where early throttle release flattens the exit arc. Goal partially met; setup balance needs one more tweak to unlock the last tenth.
Overview · VehicleSetup reacted well to the 22 °C ambient. Rear axle stiffness appropriate for this temperature window. Rear pressures climbed +1.1 psi over run — slightly high, indicating cold target could come down 0.5 psi. Front behavior consistent; no significant understeer detected in data.
What went well
+0.4sBest lap improvement vs last session
−29%Consistency σ dropped significantly
T1Entry speed held well under braking
stableFront pressures stayed inside target window
goodAxle stiffness well-matched to track temp
rangeGear ratio optimal for top-speed sector
Opportunity areas
−0.14sT3 mid-corner — early throttle release
−0.09sT8 apex — same throttle pattern
L9Lock-up T5 — isolated driver error
+1.1 psiRear pressures climbing above target
softRear axle may need one step stiffer at 32 °C+
Setup change suggestions · Driver coaching
Late-apex throttle drill
Hold throttle release until front wheels are fully straight on T3 and T8 exit. Targets −0.14s per lap.
Confidence · High
T5 braking reference
Move brake marker 5m later — current lock-up is caused by trail-braking into a compression, not excess speed.
Confidence · Medium
Setup change suggestions · Vehicle changes
Cold rear pressure −0.5 psi
Hot pressures ran +1.1 above target. Bring cold RL/RR down to compensate.
Confidence · High
Rear axle SOFT → MEDIUM
At track temps above 30 °C the soft axle allows too much flex mid-corner. Expected −0.08 to −0.12s.
Confidence · Medium

The list carries search, filter chips and sort over the session cards; tapping a card opens the detail with KPIs, track map, lap list, AI feedback and the session context wizard. Solid theme background, no hero. Data and copy verbatim from the mock — the detail intentionally shows its no-GPS / no-lap-data empty states.

FeedbackRe-run · 5 cr
Overview · DriverSolid session — best lap improved by 0.4s vs previous visit. Consistency σ dropped from 0.31 to 0.22. Main time loss sits in mid-corner on T3 and T8 where early throttle release flattens the exit arc. Goal partially met; setup balance needs one more tweak to unlock the last tenth.
Overview · VehicleSetup reacted well to the 22 °C ambient. Rear axle stiffness appropriate for this temperature window. Rear pressures climbed +1.1 psi over run — slightly high, indicating cold target could come down 0.5 psi. Front behavior consistent; no significant understeer detected in data.
What went well
+0.4sBest lap improvement vs last session
−29%Consistency σ dropped significantly
T1Entry speed held well under braking
stableFront pressures stayed inside target window
goodAxle stiffness well-matched to track temp
rangeGear ratio optimal for top-speed sector
Opportunity areas
−0.14sT3 mid-corner — early throttle release
−0.09sT8 apex — same throttle pattern
L9Lock-up T5 — isolated driver error
+1.1 psiRear pressures climbing above target
softRear axle may need one step stiffer at 32 °C+
Setup change suggestions · Driver coaching
Late-apex throttle drill
Hold throttle release until front wheels are fully straight on T3 and T8 exit. Targets −0.14s per lap.
Confidence · High
T5 braking reference
Move brake marker 5m later — current lock-up is caused by trail-braking into a compression, not excess speed.
Confidence · Medium
Setup change suggestions · Vehicle changes
Cold rear pressure −0.5 psi
Hot pressures ran +1.1 above target. Bring cold RL/RR down to compensate.
Confidence · High
Rear axle SOFT → MEDIUM
At track temps above 30 °C the soft axle allows too much flex mid-corner. Expected −0.08 to −0.12s.
Confidence · Medium

FeedbackRe-run · 5 cr
Overview · DriverSolid session — best lap improved by 0.4s vs previous visit. Consistency σ dropped from 0.31 to 0.22. Main time loss sits in mid-corner on T3 and T8 where early throttle release flattens the exit arc. Goal partially met; setup balance needs one more tweak to unlock the last tenth.
Overview · VehicleSetup reacted well to the 22 °C ambient. Rear axle stiffness appropriate for this temperature window. Rear pressures climbed +1.1 psi over run — slightly high, indicating cold target could come down 0.5 psi. Front behavior consistent; no significant understeer detected in data.
What went well
+0.4sBest lap improvement vs last session
−29%Consistency σ dropped significantly
T1Entry speed held well under braking
stableFront pressures stayed inside target window
goodAxle stiffness well-matched to track temp
rangeGear ratio optimal for top-speed sector
Opportunity areas
−0.14sT3 mid-corner — early throttle release
−0.09sT8 apex — same throttle pattern
L9Lock-up T5 — isolated driver error
+1.1 psiRear pressures climbing above target
softRear axle may need one step stiffer at 32 °C+
Setup change suggestions · Driver coaching
Late-apex throttle drill
Hold throttle release until front wheels are fully straight on T3 and T8 exit. Targets −0.14s per lap.
Confidence · High
T5 braking reference
Move brake marker 5m later — current lock-up is caused by trail-braking into a compression, not excess speed.
Confidence · Medium

Cold rear pressure −0.5 psi
Hot pressures ran +1.1 above target. Bring cold RL/RR down to compensate.
Confidence · High
Rear axle SOFT → MEDIUM
At track temps above 30 °C the soft axle allows too much flex mid-corner. Expected −0.08 to −0.12s.

Screen 07
Account
The account settings hub, reached from the Driver view. Read-only account info, privacy, plan, email notifications, privacy & tracking, data export with a 7-day cooldown, and the Danger Zone with the type-DELETE confirmation sheet. The helmet card moved to the Driver view (2.10); notification settings open as their own view (14.14). App-level preferences (appearance, language, units, preferences) moved to App settings (7.4), its own view from 2.10 Driver; language opens 14.15 from there.
Navigation between sub-blocks
2.10 Drivertap Account→7.1 AccountDelete account→7.3 Delete confirm
7.1 Accountexport < 7 days→7.2 Export cooldown
7.1 AccountManage plan→8.2 Upgrade Plan
2.10 Drivertap App settings→7.4 App settings
Sections and copy verbatim from the mock (account.html + js/account.js + css/account.css + css/shared.css botones). Seed: Driver · driver@lapkr.com · Google · member since September 15, 2024 (STRING_DEFAULT_MEMBER_SINCE) · Free plan. Privacy and email toggles default ON (hydrateToggles); consent defaults OFF except Strictly necessary locked ON (consent.js denied-by-default); Update kart data OFF. Units = metric defaults of the EN locale (OBJ_METRIC_DEFAULTS: °C · kg · psi · km/h · cm). The Install LapKr card ships hidden by default and is not represented. The Delete account modal is family lk-sheet: on mobile it drops as a bottom sheet — no ✕ per the global sheet rule (the mock DOES ship ✕, divergence registered); CTA Permanently delete disabled at 40% until DELETE is typed (initial state represented, mirror of 5.9). Export cooldown: derived date (last export Jun 10, 09:41 + 7 days). Change helmet lives at the top of the Driver view (2.10) and opens the helmet picker (pending, arrives with the user's visual reference).

Screen 08
Buy Credits & Upgrade Plan
In-app purchase surfaces. Buy Credits: five one-time packs with per-credit math, a strip of what credits buy, and the 6-month expiry note. Upgrade Plan: Free / Annual / Monthly cards plus the universal “included with every plan” and credit-based feature lists. Both open as bottom sheets over the active screen.
Navigation between sub-blocks
2.8 Drawertap 155 cr→8.1 Buy Credits←Buy Credits2.10 DriverUpgrade Plan→8.2 Upgrade Plan
10.2 · 4.23 Out of creditsTop up→8.1 Buy Credits
2.8 Drawer · 3.1 DashboardGo unlimited→8.2 Upgrade Plan
Catalog and copy verbatim from the mock (js/features/modals/util.js + i18n EN): 5 packs with a derived $/cr line (price ÷ credits) and 3 plans with Free = Current plan disabled (the seed's current plan). NOTE: in the mock's in-app sheets the featured pack (Popular) is ORANGE and the featured plan (Best Value) is BLUE — inverse of the landing pricing registered in section 03. On mobile the sheet is opaque #14141A (spec responsive.css). No ✕: the grab is the only affordance (the doc's global sheet rule; the mock ships ✕ — conscious divergence, registered). The backdrop is the Driver 2.11 view, the real origin of both rows.

Screen 09
Credits History
The append-only credit ledger. Type filter pills and a date-range select over a four-column table — date, action pill, signed change and balance after — with tap-to-expand row detail (source, reference, description) and the empty state for new accounts.
Navigation between sub-blocks
2.10 DriverCredits History→9.1 Ledgertap row→9.3 Row detail
9.1 Ledgerno activity→9.2 Empty
Table verbatim from the mock (credits-history.html + js/credits-history-page.js + css/credits-history.css): Date / Action / Change / Balance after columns, type pills colored by action, Chakra delta (− orange #FDBA74 · + teal #5EEAD4), expandable row with Source / Reference / Description + full timestamp (one expanded at a time), lazy pagination of 20 with sentinel (not represented). On mobile (≤640px) the table keeps the 4 columns with compact paddings. The mock ledger ships no seed: the rows derive from the doc seed and close row by row into the drawer's 155 cr balance (row-by-row consistency verified). The expanded detail uses the Coach Chat row (no ref — the ch_detail_no_ref case). Pill-filtered state: minor pending. release-UAT mirrors with no divergences (app/credits-history/page.tsx).

12.1 Profile · Overview←→2.1 Feed
12.1, 12.2 and 12.3 are the same surface in three states: Free plan = DNA paywall (12.1); paid plan with ≥1 analyzed session = full Driver DNA (12.2); paid plan with no AI feedback yet = profile-being-built empty state (12.3). The paywall REPLACES the overview content in the DOM (data-absent gating, not a visual veil) — a Free user with zero data still sees the upgrade CTA, never the empty state.

Driver DNA
Aggressive late-braker with strong trail-braking technique. Quick to find the optimal line on flowing tracks; struggles with throttle modulation in slow technical sections. Adapts well to wet conditions and consistently within 0.3s of best lap pace.
⚡Equipped Traits
▸Trail-braking on high-speed entries▸Lap-to-lap consistency under 0.3s σ▸Late-apex commitment in flowing corners▸Wet-line adaptation across sessions
⚠Weak Points
▸Throttle modulation in slow corners▸Tight hairpins (≥90° technical)▸Tire warm-up in first 2 laps▸Recovery pace after off-track
Recurring patterns
01T3-style late corners: −0.15s avg vs optimal
02Throttle dip at apex on slow corners
03Lap 1 cold pace deficit (every session)
04Improvement plateau on standard setup
Progression milestones
Apr 2026Throttle precision graduated to moderate
Mar 2026Cornering score +0.8 after seat-position change
Feb 2026Consistency breakthrough (σ 0.42 → 0.28)

Screen 13
Head-to-Head
Run list with filters and result chips (WON / LOST / TIED, snapshot pill), empty state, 3-step wizard (driver, their session, your session) with empty and warning states, and the replay detail with standings, dual trace, transport, Speed/G-Force telemetry, lap deltas, sector splits, delete confirm and the no-replay defensive fallback (replay data missing or corrupt — unreachable in normal flows).
Navigation between sub-blocks
Menu ☰ (2.8)H2H→13.1 List+ New→13.4 Wizard 1Next→13.6 Wizard 2Next→13.8 Wizard 3Start · 1 cr→13.10 Replay
13.1 Listtap run card→13.10 Replay←→13.1
13.10 ReplayDelete→13.13 Confirmreplay data missing→13.14 Unavailable
13.4/13.6/13.8estados→13.7 Unpublished→13.5 / 13.9 Empty
13.2 is the same surface as 13.1 for an account with no runs. The replay stage is represented with the dual SVG trace — the map-vs-SVG DECISION queue (DIVERGENCIAS #1) remains open and the doc does not prejudge it. Registered: the H2H button on a Feed card will open this wizard with the rival preselected (skips step 1). Mock bug represented as fixed: Your best / Opponent best showed "undefined". Start = Start · 1 cr (fixed, it previously said Start H2H — a doc invention). The replay's Fastest lap tile only shows when YOU hold the fastest lap (Tanaka holds it in this run, so it does not appear). Still unrepresented: filtered list with no results ("No H2Hs match your search.") and the "No sector data" fallback when GPS is missing — registered as pending.
